tob-10823: Lucifer was the monthly magazine of the Theosophical Society, edited by Helena Blavatsky herself. Its first volume carries her essays on occultism and Eastern philosophy alongside contributions from early Theosophists. The title — ‘light-bringer’ — proclaimed the magazine’s mission to spread esoteric wisdom. It is a primary document of the late-Victorian occult revival.
tob-4023: Voltaire’s biting little satire trails the innocent Candide through war, quake, and human folly, jeering at the sages who called this ‘the best of all possible worlds.’ Each calamity is funnier and blacker than the last. The book’s closing counsel — ‘we must tend our garden’ — ranks among literature’s most famous last lines.
tob-11023: Vatsyayana’s Kama Sutra is far more than its name’s naughtiness — an old Indian handbook on the art of living well: love, wooing, house-keeping, and town manners. Set down near the third century, it counts delight among life’s rightful aims. This rendering gives the whole text.
tob-11123: The old Indian classic of love and the good life, here in a second Englishing. Vatsyayana’s work takes in all — wooing and wedding, the ordering of a well-kept house — pleasure sought with taste and bridle. Its plain speech on longing made it famed; its wisdom on living well earns equal fame.
tob-13323: Benham’s Imitation of Christ turns à Kempis’s ageless handbook — its counsels on lowliness, patience in trial, and love of the holy meal — into flowing Victorian prose. Six hundred years it has led Christians toward the inward life. This rendering kept it dear to English readers.
tob-0123: William Reed’s 1906 book argues the earth is hollow, with vast polar mouths opening on a warm inner world. He claimed explorers’ tales of warm winds and stray greenery proved his case. The book is a classic of hollow-earth lore, dear to fringe thinkers ever since.
tob-4123: Kashinath Telang’s Sacred Books volume gives the Bhagavad-Gita with Sanatsugatiya and Anugita — Krishna’s word with Sanskrit text and notes. His careful learning served the great series well. Victorian readers met the Gita in trusty English dress. The volume opened Hindu wisdom to the West.
tob-4223: Agrippa’s Three Books — 1533 — are the wonder-books’ wonder-book, binding star-lore, Kabbalah, and ghost-raising in one vast frame. The bold German scholar’s toil schooled every wonder-worker after. This printing gives the classic text. The books stay western wonder-craft’s ground.
tob-10623: The Book of the Gate is ancient Egypt’s funerary text — the sun god’s perilous journey through the twelve gates of the night. Inscribed in pharaohs’ tombs, it guided the dead toward rebirth. The work is a cornerstone of Egyptian afterlife literature.
cia-0000104823: An early Cold War document, estimated to date from 1948, on the Office of Policy Coordination — the CIA's first covert-action arm, which ran secret political operations abroad. It covers the office's formative years, when America was inventing its peacetime spy toolkit. Historians treasure such records because they open a door onto the very start of CIA covert operations.
cia-0000109823: An operational report covering noon Thursday, October 18, to noon Thursday, October 26 — the archive dates the document itself September 1945, an apparent mismatch. Week-long operational summaries were the routine pulse of intelligence work. Even with its confused dates, the entry preserves the rhythm of spying in 1945.
cia-0000119723: A September 1956 report on top Hungarian party leaders planning to visit Belgrade. Tito's Yugoslavia was the model for independent communism, and Hungarian reformers wanted a look. The document captures the moment before the storm — reformers seeking inspiration, weeks before Soviet tanks answered.
cia-0000122523: A January 1992 report on Iraqi biological weapons mission planning — filed after the Gulf War exposed Saddam's arsenal. BW meant germ weapons: anthrax, botulinum, and the plans to use them. The document shows the hunt for Iraq's hidden programs entering its forensic phase.
cia-0000132423: Item 10 in the January 1960 series: the Cuban government planning further drastic state controls — the truncated title cuts off the sectors. Nationalizations were coming, and the economy with them. The document foresees the takeover: the state, swallowing business.
cia-0000132623: A June 1960 report, its title carrying the archive's typo, on Khrushchev's assurances encouraging anti-American Cuban leaders — and more, the truncated title suggests. Moscow's backing emboldened Havana's hardliners. The document is the green light: the patron, encouraging.
cia-0000135823: A 1954 LINCOLN contact report. Contacts were the operation's lifelines — agents, informants, go-betweens. The document is the meeting, reported: the contact, debriefed.
cia-0000135923: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting contacts made in Washington. The headquarters worked its own capital. The document is the networking: the contacts, made — in Washington.
cia-0000136123: The situation report for May 3 to 10, 1954. The May watch. The document is the week: the situation, reported.
cia-0000137323: The record of the 362nd NSC briefing on April 14, 1959, with attached documents titled Report — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The spring briefing's reports. The document is the session: the 362nd, documented.
cia-0000139023: A 1946 military information report: Mukden looted by the Russian army. The Manchurian city's stripping, witnessed. The document is the loot: the city, plundered.
cia-0000139323: A 1943 memo to Whitney H. Shepardson titled Attention Mr. Goldberg, on the Moscow something — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The wartime OSS correspondence. The document is the memo: the attention, directed.

un-ga-res-56-223: General Assembly Resolution 56/223, adopted in 2002 during the 56th session — aligned. The post-9/11 Assembly at work. The designation and year are certain; the subject belongs to the text.

cia-0000135723: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135723. The training year's papers — before the beaches. The document is the before: the brigade, preparing.

cia-0000136723: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136723. The training year's papers, firm-dated. The document is the training: the papers, early.
plos-pone-0000023: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper on developing a tumor-selective approach to treat metastatic cancer. Killer cells aimed only at tumors, sparing healthy tissue. The paper is the targeting: the cancer, selected — the body, spared.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d23: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, August 11, 1943 — Document 23. A second letter the same day. The message is the doubling: the day, busy.

frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d423: The minister in Iran, Dreyfus, to the Secretary of State, December 8, 1943 — Document 423. More from Tehran. The cable is the more: Dreyfus, again.
arxiv-2605-08823: The Riegel–Crutcher cloud is a cold wisp of gas near the galactic center, and magnetic fields may have sculpted its shape. Gabriel A. P. Franco and coauthors map the cloud in optical polarization: starlight passing through aligned dust grains reveals the magnetic field's direction across the sky. The 2026 paper reads the magnetic fingerprint written across the cloud.
arxiv-2605-09223: Hour-long videos drown models in frames; most of them are boring. Mehrajul Abadin Miraj, Abdul Mohaimen Al Radi, Shariful Islam, and colleagues sample events instead, regulated by curvature, in CREST. The 2026 paper makes long-video understanding efficient by watching only what matters.
arxiv-2605-09323: Phonons — quantized sound waves in crystals — are usually taught as masses on springs, but geometry offers a deeper language. Aleksey Prots formulates phonons in crystalline phases bundle-theoretically, treating vibrations as geometric objects. The 2026 paper is mathematical physics at its most elegant: sound as shape.
arxiv-2605-09423: Embodied AI agents need worlds to practice in, and hand-building them does not scale. Haoqiang Kang, Xiaokang Ye, Yuhan Liu, and colleagues generate environments automatically with an evolving coding agent — SimWorld Studio. The 2026 paper is a world-factory for robot training.
arxiv-2605-09623: Running neural networks across the edge-cloud continuum means splitting them adaptively — some layers here, some there. Akuen Akoi Deng, Eimantas Butkus, Alfreds Lapkovskis, and colleagues partition and offload DNNs adaptively. The 2026 paper is systems research for the computing continuum.
arxiv-2605-09723: Isolated neutron stars cool over eons, and exotic interior matter — hyperons, kaon condensates — changes the cooling rate measurably. Bhavnesh Bhat, Akira Dohi, Takumi Muto, and Tsuneo Noda model the cooling process. The 2026 paper is nuclear astrophysics on stellar refrigerators everywhere.
arxiv-2605-09823: Multi-agent LLMs must coordinate to solve hard tasks — but coordination leaks information, and privacy demands silence. Chelsea Zou, Yiheng Yao, Selena She, and colleagues evaluate the coordination-privacy tradeoff with CalBench. The 2026 paper measures exactly what teamwork costs in privacy.
plos-pone-0003423: Vaccine researchers tried a mirror trick against HIV in this 2008 animal study. Instead of using the virus itself, they built anti-idiotype antibodies that mimic the CD4-binding site HIV grabs onto, then injected them into rabbits. The rabbits mounted an anti-HIV response to the mimic, a creative step toward vaccines that teach the immune system to block the virus's grip.
plos-pone-0003523: Molecular biologists ruled out two suspects in this 2008 paper. The PCNA gene, essential for DNA copying, ramps up under estrogen, and two nearby estrogen response elements looked like the cause. Knocking them out changed nothing, proving those sequences are not responsible and sending the hunt for the real mechanism back to the drawing board.
plos-pone-0003623: Microbiologists Tucker, Hicks, Clarke, and colleagues caught a bacterial sensor feeling nitric oxide directly in this 2008 paper. The repressor NsrR detects the toxic gas through an iron-sulfur cluster built into the protein itself. The direct molecular touch explains how diverse bacteria sense and survive the immune system's chemical weapon.
plos-pone-0003723: In 2008, Noel, Mehta, and Zhu worked to save babies born to HIV-positive mothers in Haiti. At the GHESKIO clinic in Port-au-Prince, the team tracked efforts to improve infant outcomes in a resource-poor setting. The study measures what it takes to break the chain of mother-to-child transmission.
plos-pone-0003823: In 2008, Dettman and Justice fingered a gene in mouse lymphomas. The zinc finger SET domain gene Prdm14 was overexpressed in lymphoblastic lymphomas carrying retroviral insertions. The finding, from cancer-prone AKXD mouse strains, nominates Prdm14 as a player in blood cancers.
plos-pone-0003923: In 2008, Wilson, Ott, and Quick found space germs obeying their soup. Salmonella grown in spaceflight changed its virulence, but the surrounding ions called the tune. The ion makeup of the growth medium controlled the bacterium's regulatory and virulence responses. The result matters for astronaut health and for understanding infection-like stress.
plos-pone-0004023: In 2008, Susanto, Lin, and Chen tied stem-cell youth to porphyrin balance. The ABCG2 transporter kept porphyrin balance steady in young embryonic stem cells. Proper porphyrin handling proved necessary for continued stem-cell self-renewal cycles. This metabolic housekeeping reveals a surprising new pillar supporting pluripotency in cells.
plos-pone-0004123: In 2009, Dyer, Maupas, and de Andrade Melo traced clumsiness after stroke. Signaling in mixed spinal pathways shifted after stroke and tracked motor incoordination. Reflex routes between paired muscle groups clearly rewired. The new map points rehab at the right circuits.
plos-pone-0004223: In 2009, Dupouy, Viardot-Foucault, and Alifano tied a gut-brain signal to human breast cancer. The neurotensin receptor-1 pathway fueled human ductal breast cancer progression directly. Blocking the receptor slowed tumor advance in mice. The pathway marks a new breast-cancer drug target.
plos-pone-0004323: In 2009, Wu, Arzeno, and Shen found chaos in healthy human heartbeats. Heart rate variability showed chaotic signatures across health, aging, and heart failure. The healthy heart beat a little less predictably. The neat finding reframes what a good rhythm means.
plos-pone-0351523: Parents decide whether kids play sports — and their perceptions rule the decision. This study explored parental perceptions of children’s physical activity: satisfaction, school-based engagement, barriers to participation, and preferences. The findings show what keeps kids on the couch and what finally gets them moving.
plos-pone-0358323: Standard eye charts don’t capture real reading ability in people with low vision. This Japanese disability evaluation cohort study tested the functional acuity score as a surrogate of reading performance. The score could reshape how disability is evaluated — measuring what patients can actually do, not just what they can see.
plos-pone-0357923: COPD inflammation doesn’t always read the same way on different tests. This paper described an inflammatory discordance phenotype: a dissociation between the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and conventional inflammatory markers. The mismatch matters because it changes how doctors judge whether a patient is flaring.
plos-pone-0356623: The single-versus-multi-bedroom debate in stroke rehabilitation finally has an answer: hybrid rooms. This paper showed hybrid room designs meet stroke rehabilitation needs better than either extreme. The evidence gives hospital architects a clear brief for wards that heal.
plos-pone-0357023: School nurses in Nepal turned children into health messengers against diabetic eye disease. This quasi-experimental study tested a school health nurse-supported child-to-family strategy for diabetic retinopathy prevention in Bhimeshwor Municipality. The strategy multiplies one nurse’s reach through entire families.
plos-pone-0357123: LGBTQ+ people in Vietnam face elevated suicide risk that demands honest measurement. This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and associated factors of suicidal ideation, plans, and attempts. The data are a call for support services that affirm rather than erase.
plos-pone-0355623: Getting HIV PrEP to the women who need it most requires changing organizations, not just individuals. The EUPHORIA protocol outlines a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial testing uptake strategies for PrEP ‘for her’. The planned trial aims to scale prevention where it’s been failing.
plos-pone-0349423: Thailand’s unconditional child support grant puts cash directly in families’ hands — but does it change children’s lives? This paper examined the grant’s outcomes on children. The findings give social policymakers hard evidence about whether unconditional cash delivers.
plos-pone-0356723: Across the Ediacaran-Cambrian transition — when complex life exploded — continents weathered and phosphorus cycled in lockstep. This paper studied that continental weathering-phosphogenesis coupling in southwestern China. The geochemistry illuminates the environmental stage on which animal life debuted.
plos-pone-0356823: Lying leaves fingerprints in language — even in headlines. This cross-corpus study hunted linguistic markers of deception in Arabic news headlines, analyzing stylistic and numeric features across collections. The markers it found could help readers, journalists, and algorithms spot manipulated news in the Arabic-speaking world.
plos-pone-0355723: A cell’s resting membrane potential governs everything it does — and dielectrophoresis can estimate it without electrodes. This paper developed dielectrophoretic estimation of resting membrane potential in excitable cells. The contactless technique opens new windows into cellular electrophysiology.
plos-pone-0354723: Europe can’t protect freshwater biodiversity it can’t measure. This paper assessed the availability and representativeness of freshwater macroinvertebrate data for Europe-wide biodiversity trend assessment. The data audit reveals where monitoring suffices — and the vast gaps where insect declines go unrecorded.
plos-pone-0354823: Caring for an autistic child exhausts families — and they need evidence-based support. This paper developed an evidence-informed psychosocial intervention program for caregiver burden through a multi-stage process. The carefully built program gives clinicians something rare: a tested toolkit for the caregivers everyone forgets.
plos-pone-0355223: COVID-19’s variants may have affected pregnancies differently — but the evidence was fragmented. This paper associated COVID-19 by variant period with delivery-related outcomes across the United States. The variant-specific findings inform obstetric care in future pandemic waves.
plos-pone-0351623: Karst aquifers — riddled with caves and channels — discharge springs in maddeningly complex patterns. This paper modeled spring discharge in a dynamic karst aquifer using multivariate models and spectral analysis. The data-driven modeling tames karst complexity — improving water supply predictions for millions.
europmc-pmc2799523: Brain scans of epilepsy patients show more than damaged spots, they show rewired networks. This 2010 paper uses functional MRI to study how brain regions connect in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy. The authors find the normal small-world organization of brain networks is altered. The work suggests epilepsy is a disorder of whole-brain wiring, not just one bad spot.
europmc-pmc2805623: Can a cancer patient's own report of their quality of life predict how long they will live? This 2009 review gathers the literature from 1982 to 2008 on quality-of-life scores as survival predictors. The author finds that these self-reported measures often carry real prognostic weight. The overview supports taking patients' own assessments seriously in cancer care.
europmc-pmc2806523: Fruit flies stop eating at certain life stages, yet keep growing. This 2009 paper shows a fly insulin-like peptide drives that growth during nonfeeding periods. The authors trace how the peptide signals tissues to keep building. The discovery reveals a clever hormonal workaround for growing without food, with echoes in how all animals regulate growth.
europmc-pmc2820523: The weed Arabidopsis thaliana dots several lands, and this 2010 paper gauges how its groups split. The team scans gene variants across its range to map group shape. Their chart shows how place molds the weed's genes. The work set the yardstick for gene studies of this lab weed.
europmc-pmc2830923: Parasites and hosts evolve together, and reading their shared past is a tough puzzle. This 2010 paper brings Jane, a tool that lines up host and parasite family trees. The authors show how it draws the match. The program gave researchers a handy way to study joint evolution.
europmc-pmc2918523: Bones strengthen with the right exercise, and this 2010 review prescribes it. The authors systematically review targeted exercise against osteoporosis for optimizing bone strength through life. Their pooling backs weight-bearing work at every age. The review guides lifelong bone care for young and old.
europmc-pmc2966423: The brain's vessel walls have their own gene program. This 2010 paper maps the mouse blood-brain barrier transcriptome as a resource for understanding brain endothelial cells. The authors' atlas reveals the barrier's machinery. Their resource aids neurovascular research. Drug designers study it to sneak past the barrier.
europmc-pmc2978323: Skewed data complicates meta-analysis, and this 2008 paper offers a fix. The authors show how to combine results reported on log-transformed or raw scales. Their method rescues skewed studies. The work became a meta-analysis staple. Reviewers now accept mixed-scale pooling.
europmc-pmc2996323: Much of our DNA sits under evolutionary guard. This 2010 paper uses the GERP++ tool to find genome stretches kept unchanged by selection. The authors reveal hidden importance in so-called junk. Their work reframed DNA debates. Disease hunters now scan these guarded zones.
europmc-pmc3022523: Digital health's promises needed checking. This 2011 review weighs what eHealth does for care quality and safety. The authors find mixed evidence at best. Their work tempered digital hype. Glossy apps often lack proof, they find. Safety gains appear mainly in prescribing.
europmc-pmc3057423: Headache impact got a validated measure. This 2011 paper confirms the HIT-6 quiz works for episodic and chronic migraine. The authors validate the tool across groups. Their work aids headache care. Six questions capture the burden. Doctors track treatment gains with it.
europmc-pmc3080923: Flu seasons got mapped worldwide. This 2011 paper unites flu-season patterns from temperate and tropical zones. The authors' synthesis guides shot timing. Their work shaped vaccine policy. Tropics get year-round drizzles of flu. The map tells each region when to vaccinate.
europmc-pmc3091323: Gene info got a one-stop portal. This 2009 paper brings BioGPS, a hub for gene data from many sources. The authors' site became a daily tool. Their work opened genomics to all. Millions of queries flow through yearly. The portal now covers human and mouse.
europmc-pmc3095423: TB meets its immune match. This 2011 review surveys how innate immune sensors spot the tuberculosis germ. The authors map the detection web. Their overview guides vaccine design. The germ fights back with decoys. New vaccines aim to sharpen detection.
europmc-pmc6518823: Studies linking DNA methylation to disease are booming, but the statistics are easy to get wrong. This guidance paper distills hard-won lessons from the widely used Illumina EPIC array, which measures methylation at nearly a million sites. It covers study design, batch effects, and analysis traps, giving researchers a practical playbook for results they can trust.
europmc-pmc6593623: Drugs with anticholinergic effects - many bladder pills, antihistamines, and antidepressants - fog thinking in the short term. But does years of use raise dementia risk? Tracking UK patients in a nested case-control study, researchers linked heavier long-term exposure to higher dementia odds. The findings urge caution with these common medicines.
europmc-pmc6651423: The NLRP3 inflammasome is the immune system's tripwire for cellular damage - sensing danger and unleashing fiery inflammation. This overview explains how it switches on, how the body restrains it, and what goes wrong in disease. Few immune sensors match its reach across gout, Alzheimer's, and more.
europmc-pmc6769923: Finding a drug used to mean screening millions of compounds by hand - now computers dock them first. This review covers molecular docking's shifting paradigms: predicting how ligands grip their targets and what makes a hit worth chasing. The in silico shortcut keeps reshaping discovery.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-23: This 2007 GAO report finds the State Department's get-out plans for its far-flung posts needed work. With embassies dotting shaky regions, GAO asked if the exit drills were real, fresh, and fit for a true crisis. The report lists the soft spots — and warns that a bad plan only shows its cracks when the shooting starts.
gao-gaoreports-b-299923: K9 Operations took its August 2007 dog-team contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's pick was unfair; the call tests the protest and rules. Even the government buys guard dogs by the rulebook — and GAO enforces it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-923: Chernobyl's crumbling sarcophagus needed a new cover in 2007 — and GAO's report says the shelter project was slipping behind. The findings track the delays dogging the international effort to entomb the reactor. The report is a slow-motion alarm: the world's worst nuclear scar still waited for its shield.
gao-gaoreports-b-299523: Head Inc. took its June 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest. Short name, full hearing: every bidder gets the same fair-play ruling.
gao-gaoreports-b-299723: Forensic Quality Services-International took its May 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the claims against procurement law. Even forensic deals get the full fair-play hearing in the protest system.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-523: American school aid abroad needed better teamwork and scorecards in 2007 — GAO's report calls for tighter coordination and real results measures. The findings demand proof of learning gains. The report's standard: chalk and books bought with tax dollars should show learning.
openalex-w7206151423: Artificial intelligence is entering classrooms, and this article asks what it means for students with disabilities. The authors review the teaching possibilities AI opens up, the ethical limits that must be respected, and the conditions schools need so digital tools genuinely help every student participate and learn. Balanced rather than boosterish, it treats inclusion as the test of whether classroom AI is worth having.
openalex-w7204939723: Police work is going airborne in northern Brazil. This article examines how the military police of Para are putting drones to work: surveillance, search operations, and monitoring hard-to-reach areas. The authors place the technology within the broader digital revolution reshaping public security. Part technology survey, part institutional case study, it shows what happens when a state police force adopts eyes in the sky.
openalex-w7128498023: Immune thrombocytopenia thins the blood's clotting cells, and bleeding shapes daily life. This study linked bleeding severity to quality of life in adults with ITP. The authors measured how symptoms erode well-being. A patient-centered study of a rare blood disorder's real cost.
pmc-13456823: A 2026 bibliometric review mapping the world's research on psychiatric emergency medicine from 2014 to 2023. By counting and connecting publications, the authors show which topics, countries, and collaborations grew fastest. The landscape view helps funders and researchers see where the field is heading.
pmc-13450123: In this 2026 prospective study, stroke patients who received early rehabilitation integrating traditional Chinese medicine recovered function better than those on standard care alone. The pragmatic design — run in real clinics, not artificial trial conditions — makes the results directly relevant to practice. It is evidence that early, combined rehab pays off.
pmc-13439723: A 2026 study finding that alcohol-induced early liver injury in mice leads to more voluntary drinking and cognitive deficits. The liver damage came first and worsened both behavior and thinking — a vicious cycle. The result suggests liver health and brain function are linked earlier in alcohol use than assumed.
pmc-13402023: This 2026 physiology paper with a refreshingly honest title concludes: we do not know whether head-up sleep enhances erythropoiesis — red blood cell production. The authors reviewed the evidence for the claimed effect and found it wanting. Negative conclusions like this keep the field honest.
pmc-13401723: In this 2026 rheumatology paper, interleukin-40 emerged as a treatment-sensitive marker of immune modulation — rather than disease activity — in systemic sclerosis. The distinction matters: the marker tracks what therapy is doing, not how sick the patient is. It could become a tool for monitoring treatment response.
pmc-13449223: In this 2026 paper, researchers built an integrated Raman spectroscopy platform with embedded AI for real-time cancer detection during surgery. The surgeon gets an instant molecular read on tissue margins. The AI-embedded platform is designed for the operating room, not the lab.
pmc-13332323: This 2026 review maps the downstream pathways of dystrophin deficiency in Duchenne muscular dystrophy — what goes wrong after the missing protein — and the implications for muscle degeneration and regeneration. Understanding the cascade beyond dystrophin itself opens new therapeutic angles.
pmc-13273923: This 2026 pharmacoepidemiology paper tracked lithium dispensing patterns in Dutch youth from 2011 to 2022 — prevalence, incidence, dosages, and duration. Lithium in young people is carefully watched. The decade-long trends inform prescribing policy.
pmc-13439923: A 2026 (listed 2025) paper on the nanosd integral gene drive enabling population modification of Anopheles gambiae — the malaria mosquito. Gene drives could transform malaria control. The integral drive design is the advance.
pmc-13467823: This 2026 food science paper studied rheological profile and bioactive compounds in yogurt with cherry plum powder. The fruit addition changed texture and nutrition. The formulation is the contribution.
pmc-13424523: A 2026 study of the relationship between non-O blood groups and microvascular risk in type 2 diabetes. Blood type may modulate small-vessel complications. The association is the finding.
pmc-13490923: This 2026 dental materials paper tested fracture resistance of thermally-mechanically aged resin composite-restored premolars under different universal adhesive protocols. The aging simulation was the rigor. The protocols were compared.
pmc-13449623: A 2026 Canadian study of communication barriers and facilitators to specialist pediatric palliative care involvement in pediatric oncology settings. The referral obstacles were mapped. The facilitators guide improvement.
pmc-13442923: A 2026 glioblastoma paper on harnessing repurposed drugs to enhance temozolomide efficacy. The old drugs boosted the chemo. The harnessing is the strategy.
pmc-13435823: A 2026 qualitative paper on experiences and perceptions of occupational therapy and physiotherapy practice education in research settings. The students' research placements were explored. The perceptions inform education.
pmc-13433823: This 2026 statistics paper estimated microbial diversity and calculated Hill numbers using the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process. The Bayesian method handled the diversity. The process is the tool.
pmc-13420923: A 2026 paper developing and validating the WORC-PAIN questionnaire — 'Working With Chronic Pain: Assessment of Impacts' — for people in paid work with chronic pain (the title is truncated). The work-focused pain measure was validated. The questionnaire is the tool.

pmc-13524623: A 2026 deep learning paper on multi-class semantic segmentation of oral cancer tissues on whole-slide images — a SuperPixel-enhanced approach. The AI mapped the cancer. The segmentation aids pathologists.
pmc-13443523: This 2026 paper addressed mpox research coordination to support response efforts in Africa — lessons learned, challenges, and way forward. The coordination was evaluated. The lessons guide the next outbreak.
pmc-13430523: A 2026 natural products paper discovering sugarnitriles A and B and structurally reassigning SF-2140 from a sugarcane endophytic actinomycete. The microbial chemistry was decoded. The discovery is the contribution.
pmc-13428123: In this 2026 study, the impact of giant cell arteritis and glucocorticoid treatment on health-related quality of life was measured. The vasculitis's life toll was quantified. The measurement informs care.
pmc-13428023: A 2026 case report of recalcitrant pemphigus vulgaris treated with rituximab. The stubborn blistering disease yielded to the biologic. The case supports the therapy.
pmc-13426023: In this 2026 mosquito paper, interactions between inbreeding, fitness, and the bacterial microbiome were studied in Aedes aegypti. The inbred mosquitoes' microbes mattered. The interactions are the ecological insight.
pmc-13503923: A 2026 editorial, "Altering our (soils') future." The soil's future was the subject. The editorial is the call to action.
pmc-13427723: In this 2026 paper, a game-theoretic attack-defense framework was built for studying network resilience. The cyber conflict was modeled. The framework is the analytical tool.
pmc-13579223: A 2026 materials paper: "De Novo Autogenic Engineered Living Functional Materials." The living materials were built from scratch. The paper is the advance.
pmc-13473023: A 2026 paper on humanizing the pediatric intensive care unit through new technologies and artificial intelligence. The high-tech PICU's human side was addressed. The humanizing is the agenda.
pmc-13443823: In this 2026 South African study, utilization of procedural sedation and analgesia was examined at a regional hospital emergency department in KwaZulu-Natal. The sedation practices were audited. The utilization data inform the ED.
pmc-13532823: In this 2026 physiology paper, presentation of preload and afterload to isolated heart preparations was described. The cardiac mechanics teaching was the contribution. The presentation serves educators.
pmc-13461323: A 2026 machine learning study exploring predictors of analgesic response in adult women regularly using NSAIDs. The AI predicted the pain relief. The insights personalize analgesia.
arxiv-2606-16023: People's movement patterns — where they go and when — can reveal unusual behavior, but most detection systems can't explain their verdicts. IBAD is an interpretable system that flags behavioral anomalies in human mobility data and shows its reasoning in understandable terms. The authors present the method for researchers working on location data and public safety.
arxiv-2606-16423: A factory must decide how much to produce when delivery lead times are uncertain but bounded by a budget of uncertainty. This operations-research paper solves the single-item lot-sizing problem under that budgeted uncertainty. It targets supply-chain researchers seeking production plans that stay robust when suppliers are late.
arxiv-2606-16523: AI agents are collecting "skills" — reusable abilities — faster than anyone can organize them. SkillWiki proposes a living knowledge infrastructure for agent skills: a wiki-like system where skills are documented, shared, and kept current. The paper targets researchers building the ecosystem of capable AI agents.
arxiv-2606-16723: AI agents now act in the world — booking, buying, deciding. Do they treat people unfairly when they act? AgentFairBench is a test suite that checks whether LLM agents discriminate in their actions. The paper gives fairness researchers a standard way to probe agent bias.
